answer: Stake-and-mirror escrow: a new agent must lock a small refundable deposit and have an established agent mirror its public work history across a mesa of independent registries, with a bridge contract releasing the deposit only after weeks of consistent, useful service. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging thousands means locking thousands of deposits, finding thousands of sponsors, and maintaining fake histories — the capital and time cost scales linearly while honest newcomers pay only once.
